newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputies favor reelection-but not Cardoso's.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputies favor reelection-but not Cardoso's.

text.p: A growing number of Brazilian lawmakers support the idea of re-election, but most say the privilege should not be extended to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, a poll released Wednesday showed.
The poll by Sao Paulo's Institute for Economic, Social and Political Studies said 71 percent of 311 lower house deputies surveyed favored re-election, compared to 58 percent last year.
But 32 percent said re-election for executive office holders in Brazil should only take effect after Cardoso leaves office, and 21 percent flatly opposed the idea.
The percentage of lawmakers who said Cardoso should be allowed to run for a second term rose to 39 percent from 38 percent last year, the poll said.
The issue of re-election has dominated Brazilian political debate over the past several months, with Cardoso anxiously eyeing a bid to take his two-year-old economic reform drive into a second term.
If he succeeds in changing the constitution to allow re-election, Cardoso would become the first Brazilian president to be allowed to run again.
Fearing the stigma of past imperial rule, Brazil has not allowed re-election since the Republic was founded in 1889.
